findings.title: Incorrect rarefaction fans
findings.source_locator: Equation(4.5) p18; Sections4.4-4.5 p20; Theorem2.2/Propositions2.4-2.5 pp8-10
findings.common_hypotheses_tex:
\section{Identity, hypotheses, and scope}
The reviewed source is Sunder Sethuraman and S.R.S.\ Varadhan, \emph{Atypical behaviors of a tagged particle in asymmetric simple exclusion}, arXiv:2311.07800v1, submitted 13 November 2023, 39 PDF pages \cite{sv}. The first page carries the internal date 15 November 2023. The assignment associates this work with DOI \url{10.1214/24-AOP1752}; that bibliographic association is not a certificate of equality with the journal text. All page locators below refer to the frozen preprint, whose printed and PDF page numbers agree.

The process is nearest-neighbor exclusion on $\mathbb Z$, with $p\in(1/2,1]$, $q=1-p$, $\gamma=p-q>0$, density $\rho\in(0,1)$, and a particle pinned at the origin. The observation time is $N$, and the deviation threshold is $A$. Results for negative $A$ require $q>0$; the nonentropic lower-tail construction is proved only for TASEP. The main explicit upper-tail rate is
\[
 I_\gamma(A)=
 \begin{cases}
 A\log\!\dfrac{A}{\gamma(1-\rho)}-A+\gamma(1-\rho),
       &\gamma(1-\rho)<A<\gamma,\\[3pt]
 I^Z(A)-A\log(1-\rho)-\gamma\rho,&A\geq\gamma,
 \end{cases}
\quad
 I^Z(A)=A\log c-pc-q/c+1,
\]
where $c=(A+\sqrt{A^2+4pq})/(2p)$. The boundary value at the typical speed is understood by continuity.

For profiles vanishing at the origin, conditioning on $\eta(0)=1$ must mean the pinned product law
\[
 \delta_1(d\eta(0))\bigotimes_{x\ne0}\operatorname{Bern}
       \bigl(\rho_0(x/N)\bigr).
\]
Literal conditioning on a null event does not define that law. Under this intended interpretation, the Radon--Nikodym product on p.~22 omits $x=0$; its printed extra factor is an order-one normalization error and does not change an $N$-scale entropy. Compact truncations, integer threshold conventions, and the order $N\to\infty$ before the truncation radius tends to infinity are also operative.
findings.complete_evidence_tex:
\begin{problem}[Major: several printed rarefaction profiles do not solve the conservation law]
Equation (4.5), p.~18, and the displayed evolutions in Sections 4.4 and 4.5, p.~20, are asserted to be entropic solutions of
\begin{equation}\label{burgers}
 \partial_t r+\gamma(1-2r)\partial_u r=0.
\end{equation}
Their rarefaction branches fail this equation even at smooth interior points. The first two profiles are used to identify the typical tagged position in the changed measure.
\end{problem}
\begin{proof}
In (4.5), take $\gamma=\rho=1/2$ and $a=A_\epsilon=3/8$, for instance $A=5/16$, $\epsilon=1/16$. These satisfy Theorem 2.2's strict parameter restrictions. The printed boundaries are $m(t)=-t/4$, $s(t)=3t/8$, and the intervening density is
\[
 r(t,u)=\frac{2(t-u)}{5t}.
\]
Its residual in \eqref{burgers} is
\[
 \partial_t r+\tfrac12(1-2r)\partial_u r
       =-\frac{t-6u}{25t^2}.
\]
At $(t,u)=(1/2,0)$, strictly inside the fan, this equals $-2/25$. Thus the discrepancy is not a choice of shock convention or a value at a discontinuity.

For Section 4.4, choose $\gamma=\rho=1/2$ and $A_\epsilon=1/8$, realized by $A=3/16$, $\epsilon=1/3$. The printed fan is
\[
 r(t,u)=\frac{3t-2u+1}{5t},\qquad
 \partial_t r+\tfrac12(1-2r)\partial_u r
       =\frac{t+6u-3}{25t^2}.
\]
At $(1/2,1/2)$ its residual is $2/25$. For Section 4.5, take $\gamma=\rho=1/2$, $A=-1/4$, $\epsilon=1/8$ and $x_0=A-\gamma-\epsilon=-7/8$. The printed fan has residual
\[
 -\frac{4t-8u-7}{36t^2},
\]
equal to $-2/9$ at $(t,u)=(1/2,x_0)$. All three residuals were independently reproduced by symbolic differentiation.
\end{proof}

\emph{Repair and counterevidence.}
A rarefaction from left density $L$ to right density $R<L$, initially at $x_0$, has boundaries
\[
 x_0+\gamma(1-2L)t,\qquad x_0+\gamma(1-2R)t,
 \qquad
 r(t,u)=\frac12\left(1-\frac{u-x_0}{\gamma t}\right).
\]
Consequently, in (4.5) one should use
\[
 m(t)=\gamma(1-2\rho)t,\qquad s(t)=(2a-\gamma)t,
\]
while retaining the printed compression boundaries
$\ell(t)=\gamma-a+(2a-\gamma)t$ and
$r_+(t)=a-\gamma+2\gamma\rho+\gamma(1-2\rho)t$.
The trajectory $u=at$ remains in the density $1-a/\gamma$ plateau until its right endpoint at $t=1$. The left fan edge is strictly behind it, and
$\ell(t)-at=(\gamma-a)(1-t)\geq0$.

In Section 4.4 the correct fan boundaries are
$\gamma+(2a-\gamma)t$ and $\gamma+\gamma(1-2\rho)t$.
The shock from the origin has speed $a-\gamma\rho$. Before $t=1$ it has not met the fan, and the path $at$ is in the plateau. In Section 4.5 the left edge of the fan should be $x_0+\gamma(1-2\rho)t$; the right edge $x_0+\gamma t$ is already correct. The separate particle comparison on p.~21 uses this right edge.

The corrected intermediate upper-tail profile has initial entropy
\begin{align}
 &(\gamma-a)h_\rho(1-a/\gamma)
 +\int_{\gamma-a}^{a-\gamma+2\gamma\rho}
        h_\rho\!\left(\frac{u-a+\gamma}{2\gamma}\right)\,du \notag\\
 &\hspace{35mm}=a\log\frac{a}{\gamma(1-\rho)}-a+\gamma(1-\rho),\label{entropy}
\end{align}
where $h_\rho(z)=z\log(z/\rho)+(1-z)\log((1-z)/(1-\rho))$.
The cumulative-mass calculation includes the left truncation's vacuum-to-density shock; omitting that boundary flux would give an incorrect mass check. With that shock included, direct integration gives the tagged quantile $a$. Three independent high-precision integrations of \eqref{entropy} agreed with its closed form. The error invalidates the printed invocation of the hydrodynamic limit, but these repairs support the intended conclusion of Theorem 2.2 and Proposition 2.4. They do not demonstrate a false final rate function.

findings.complete_evidence_tex:
\begin{problem}[Major: the Euler--Lagrange equation ignores active derivative constraints]
Section 6.2, pp.~26--29, imposes $\epsilon\leq v'\leq1-\epsilon$, then derives an unconstrained Euler--Lagrange equality in Step 2 and (6.1) in Step 3. Under its stated assumptions that equality can be impossible for every admissible function.
\end{problem}
\begin{proof}
Use the notation of Section 6.2 and take
\[
 a=0,\quad b=1,\quad \delta=\epsilon=1/10,\quad \rho=1/2,\quad
 H(u)=u/10+u^2/1000,\quad \lambda=100.
\]
The function $H$ is smooth, strictly increasing and strictly convex, with $H(0)=0$ and $H'(1)<\rho$. Also $\epsilon\leq H'(\delta)=501/5000$, so this is within the third case of Proposition 6.1 and the specified regularization.

Every admissible $v$ has $v(\delta)\geq0$ and
$v(u)\geq(u-\delta)/10$. Hence
\[
 H(u)-v(u)\leq 1/100+u^2/1000\leq11/1000.
\]
The asserted equality $(h_\rho'(v'))'=\lambda e^{-\lambda(H-v)}$ would imply
\[
 h_\rho'(v'(1))-h_\rho'(v'(\delta))
 \geq 90e^{-1.1}>29.95.
\]
But $v'\in[1/10,9/10]$ forces the left side to be at most
$h_\rho'(9/10)-h_\rho'(1/10)=2\log9<4.40$.
The contradiction also applies to the claimed weak derivative, by integrating over interior subintervals and taking endpoints. The constrained minimizer exists by compactness and lower semicontinuity; it therefore cannot satisfy the printed equality.
\end{proof}

\emph{Dependency and repair.}
This is the foundation for the convexity and contact-set argument leading to Proposition 6.1, Proposition 2.9 and both upper bounds. A variational inequality or a proof that the constraints are inactive is required; the latter is false in the example. Thus the core derivation needs replacement.

There is direct counterevidence to a stronger allegation that the intended optimizer is wrong. For the corrected candidate $v_*$, put $\psi=h_\rho'(v_*')$. Its slope increases only while $v_*=H$, and is constant on the initial tangent and final slope-$\rho$ portions. For any admissible $w$, convexity gives
\begin{equation}\label{certificate}
 \int_a^b\!\bigl[h_\rho(w')-h_\rho(v_*')\bigr]\,du
 \geq [\psi(w-v_*)]_a^b-\int_{[a,b]}(w-v_*)\,d\psi\geq0.
\end{equation}
Here $d\psi\geq0$ is supported on the contact set, where $w-v_*\leq0$; the initial boundary difference is zero. At the right boundary either $\psi=0$ or the candidate is still on $H$ with $\psi\leq0$, giving the same sign. For the quadratic obstacle used in Proposition 2.9, a zero initial slope is handled by truncation: the remaining boundary term is $O(\delta|\log\delta|)$ and vanishes. Strict convexity gives uniqueness. This proves the required candidate optimality without the invalid regularization equation, after correcting the printed formulas below.

\section{The global upper-bound step}

findings.complete_evidence_tex:
\begin{problem}[Major: the displayed local bounds do not imply (5.7)]
Section 5.1, Step 2, p.~23, replaces a minimum containing an indicator by an infimum restricted to where that indicator is one. The preceding bound has already discarded the superexponential exclusion of the other cases. Its asserted compact cover is also not justified for the center-dependent neighborhoods used there.
\end{problem}
Let
\[
 F(\beta)=v_\beta(1,A)-v_\beta(0,0),\qquad
 J_i=\mathbf1_{\{F(\beta_i)<\epsilon+\delta\}}.
\]
The printed minimum is $\min_i J_i(K(\beta_i)-2\delta)$.
An inadmissible center contributes zero. Removing that center and taking a positive constrained infimum cannot follow from this expression: even the two values $J_1=0$, $J_2=1$, $K(\beta_2)-2\delta=1$ give $0$, not $1$. The correct local conclusion for a strictly inadmissible center is a superexponential bound, or a logarithmic indicator equal to $-\infty$, rather than the finite bound produced in (5.6).

The centers are continuous densities strictly between zero and one, while $\mathcal M_R$ contains zero and saturated densities. Density of the centers does not make arbitrary center-dependent small balls a cover: choosing each radius less than half its distance from the zero measure excludes zero from every ball. Lemma 3.4 and (5.4) permit shrinking these radii, so the cover requires an additional construction. Further, the assertion on p.~22 that $N\pi_t^N/(N+1)\in\mathcal M_R$ is false whenever the empirical measure has an atom: no positive atom satisfies $\mu([a,b])\leq b-a$ on arbitrarily short intervals. A uniform neighborhood approximation by spreading each atom over its lattice cell would give the intended asymptotic compactness.

\emph{Repair route and impact.}
One can organize the argument around neighborhoods of \emph{every} $W\in\mathcal M_R$, using the Bernoulli entropy dual formula
\[
 K(W)=\sup_{f\in C([-R,R])}
 \left\{\int f\,dW-\int_{-R}^R\log(1-\rho+\rho e^f)\,du\right\}.
\]
For each center choose a near-optimal bounded $f$, then a neighborhood where its affine entropy lower bound persists. Keep the superexponential estimate for centers with $F(W)>0$, with a separate tolerance near $F=0$. The product Bernoulli moment generating function and the uniform quenched tagged-particle bound then yield the entropy cost on the remaining neighborhoods. A finite subcover of this actual cover, followed by the lower-semicontinuity argument in Step 3, is the appropriate route to (5.7). Extension of each local flux estimate to these neighborhoods must be stated.

This repairs the logic the proof needs; it is not a claim that the displayed chain already proves it. The defect is central to Theorems 2.7--2.8 and Corollary 2.10. No counterexample to those final conclusions is given. The step profile used in this repair is $\mathbf1_{\{x\leq0\}}$, as in Proposition 3.3; the opposite inequality printed on p.~21 is a local orientation error. Also, the no-restriction assertion beyond $A+\gamma$ follows directly by adding to $\int_0^{A+\gamma}\rho_0\leq\gamma$, avoiding the unnecessary intermediate subtraction on p.~24.

\section{Local formula and hypothesis corrections}

findings.complete_evidence_tex:
\begin{problem}[Minor: the optimizer displays and the cost identity need normalization corrections]
Proposition 2.9, p.~12, has an incorrect translation in both terminal affine pieces. Theorem 2.7, p.~11, omits the initial empty-interval cost in its equality involving $K_1$. The first case of Proposition 6.1, p.~26, omits the left-endpoint translation.
\end{problem}
At $z_\rho=A+\gamma(2\rho-1)$ the printed affine piece
$\rho(u-\gamma(2\rho-1)+A)+G(\gamma(2\rho-1))$
jumps upward by $2\rho A$ from the obstacle branch. It is not even continuous and exceeds the obstacle near the join. The correct expression is
\[
 \rho(u-z_\rho)+G(z_\rho-A).
\]
This expression already appears correctly in Section 6.1, p.~26, providing direct internal counterevidence to failure of the intended optimizer. The $x$ in the initial branch of $v_2$ should likewise be $u$.

Even with the corrected optimizer,
\[
 K_1(v_*)=-\gamma\log(1-\rho)-\gamma\rho,
\quad
 I_\gamma(A)=I^Z(A)+K_1(v_*)-(A-\gamma)\log(1-\rho)
 \quad(A\geq\gamma).
\]
For $\gamma=\rho=1/2$, $A=4/5$, the missing cost is
$0.20794415416798359\ldots>0$. Formula (5.11), p.~24, and Step 6, p.~25, already include it. Finally, the zero-cost candidate in Proposition 6.1 is $\rho(u-a)$, with the corresponding obstacle condition. For example, $a=1$, $b=2$, $\rho=1/2$, $H(u)=1+u^2$ satisfies the printed assumptions but $v(u)=\rho u$ violates $v(a)=0$. These are false displayed assertions with local repairs, not a refutation of the rate after restoring the intended normalization.

\begin{problem}[Minor: the preliminary exponential martingale has the wrong sign]
The last display of Section 3.3, p.~13, subtracts the left-jump contribution inside the compensator. For $q>0$ this expression is not a martingale.
\end{problem}
Writing $a_\pm(s)=1-\eta_s(X_s\pm1)$, the correct compensator is
\[
 p(e^\lambda-1)a_+(s)+q(e^{-\lambda}-1)a_-(s).
\]
For the printed expression, under the pinned equilibrium law its expectation has derivative at zero
$2q(e^{-\lambda}-1)(1-\rho)$.
At $p=3/4$, $\rho=1/2$, $\lambda=\log2$, this is $-1/8$, whereas a martingale starting at one has constant expectation. Bounded jump rates justify the short-time generator calculation. Equation (4.3), p.~16, and the martingale actually used in Section 8, p.~33, have the correct sign. Thus the operative change-of-measure and step-profile upper bound survive this local correction.

findings.complete_evidence_tex:
\begin{problem}[Minor: the stationary error in (1.3) is incompatible with the stated initialization]
Equation (1.3), p.~3, writes $X_t=\operatorname{Poi}_t+\chi_t$, with $\operatorname{Poi}$ a Poisson process and $\chi$ stationary. Under the usual convention that the Poisson process starts at zero, and the paper's $X_0=0$, this cannot hold for genuine ASEP.
\end{problem}
At zero the equality forces $\chi_0=0$ almost surely; stationarity forces $\chi_t=0$ almost surely at every fixed time. It would follow that $X_t$ is nonnegative and Poisson. But for $q>0$, the left neighbor is empty initially with probability $1-\rho$, and
\[
 \PP_\rho(X_t=-1)=q(1-\rho)t+O(t^2)>0
\]
for sufficiently small $t$. The claimed representation therefore needs the precise initialization/error formulation of its cited approximation result. A stationary coboundary or a separately specified random offset would avoid this elementary contradiction, but neither is printed or independently verified here. The authors explicitly develop the main upper-tail argument independently of this approximation; the present finding does not refute its LLN or CLT.

findings.common_hypotheses_tex:
\section{Identity, hypotheses, and scope}
The reviewed source is Sunder Sethuraman and S.R.S.\ Varadhan, \emph{Atypical behaviors of a tagged particle in asymmetric simple exclusion}, arXiv:2311.07800v1, submitted 13 November 2023, 39 PDF pages \cite{sv}. The first page carries the internal date 15 November 2023. The assignment associates this work with DOI \url{10.1214/24-AOP1752}; that bibliographic association is not a certificate of equality with the journal text. All page locators below refer to the frozen preprint, whose printed and PDF page numbers agree.

The process is nearest-neighbor exclusion on $\mathbb Z$, with $p\in(1/2,1]$, $q=1-p$, $\gamma=p-q>0$, density $\rho\in(0,1)$, and a particle pinned at the origin. The observation time is $N$, and the deviation threshold is $A$. Results for negative $A$ require $q>0$; the nonentropic lower-tail construction is proved only for TASEP. The main explicit upper-tail rate is
\[
 I_\gamma(A)=
 \begin{cases}
 A\log\!\dfrac{A}{\gamma(1-\rho)}-A+\gamma(1-\rho),
       &\gamma(1-\rho)<A<\gamma,\\[3pt]
 I^Z(A)-A\log(1-\rho)-\gamma\rho,&A\geq\gamma,
 \end{cases}
\quad
 I^Z(A)=A\log c-pc-q/c+1,
\]
where $c=(A+\sqrt{A^2+4pq})/(2p)$. The boundary value at the typical speed is understood by continuity.

For profiles vanishing at the origin, conditioning on $\eta(0)=1$ must mean the pinned product law
\[
 \delta_1(d\eta(0))\bigotimes_{x\ne0}\operatorname{Bern}
       \bigl(\rho_0(x/N)\bigr).
\]
Literal conditioning on a null event does not define that law. Under this intended interpretation, the Radon--Nikodym product on p.~22 omits $x=0$; its printed extra factor is an order-one normalization error and does not change an $N$-scale entropy. Compact truncations, integer threshold conventions, and the order $N\to\infty$ before the truncation radius tends to infinity are also operative.
findings.complete_evidence_tex:
\begin{problem}[Minor: the introductory path large-deviation formula has the wrong sign]
The display defining the path large-deviation cost on p.~5 has
$\lim_{\delta\downarrow0}\lim_{N\to\infty}N^{-1}\log\PP(B_\delta)=K(\rho_0)+I_{\rm JV}(\rho)$.
Its right side must have a minus sign.
\end{problem}
Both displayed costs are nonnegative, whereas the left side cannot exceed zero. Choose a nonconstant smooth compact perturbation of the background density, of sufficiently small amplitude and derivative that its entropic evolution is smooth up to time one. It is among the stated nice profiles, has strictly positive initial entropy and zero entropic dynamical cost. The printed equality would assign it a positive logarithmic probability. The negative-cost convention in the main theorem statements and the entropy argument on pp.~17--19 are consistent; this introductory sign error does not invalidate those calculations.

findings.complete_evidence_tex:
\begin{problem}[Minor: the optional compactification proof uses an inadmissible generator test]
Section 7.3, p.~30, applies stationarity as $0=\E_\mu L_{\rm ZR}\zeta(k)$ for every invariant measure on the compactified space allowing $\zeta(k)=\infty$. This requires an additional domain and limiting argument.
\end{problem}
The coordinate function $\zeta(k)$ is neither bounded nor finite on that space. In particular, the point mass on the all-infinite configuration is invariant, but $L_{\rm ZR}\zeta(k)$ is not defined there by differences of coordinate values. Thus stationarity alone cannot justify the printed equalities for every invariant measure. Bounded truncations give boundary terms at infinity which must be treated, rather than silently replaced by the finite-coordinate formula.

This is a gap in the optional self-contained LLN proof, not a demonstrated false invariant-measure classification or false speed $\gamma$. The alternative cited by the paper was checked in the acquired Tracy--Widom preprint \cite{tw}, pp.~1--3. Its Theorem 2 assumes $0<p_{\rm TW}<q_{\rm TW}$ and gives tight fluctuations of $x_1(t/\gamma)+t$ on the square-root scale. Set $p_{\rm TW}=q$, $q_{\rm TW}=p$, and reflect by $X_s=1-x_1(s)$. Its initial positive-integer step becomes the required step on $x\leq0$, and $X_s/s\to\gamma$ follows for $0<q<p$. At $q=0$ the leading TASEP particle has an unobstructed rate-one Poisson clock, so the same LLN follows directly. The bounded drift and vanishing scaled martingale in Lemma 7.1 upgrade fixed-time limits to the required uniform limit. This establishes the cited route's applicability without re-proving its Fredholm asymptotics. A proof via compactification would still need bounded-test limits accounting for mass at infinity.

problems.independent_check: Direct differentiation of the printed smooth fans gives (6u-t)/(25t^2), (t+6u-3)/(25t^2), and -(4t-8u-7)/(36t^2). The interior evaluation points with gamma=rho=1/2 obey all parameter ranges. Correct Riemann speeds are gamma*(1-2r); the corrected plateau contains u=a*t until t=1.
problems.counterevidence_and_impact: The hydrodynamic-limit invocation uses a false claimed solution, a core lower-bound derivation. For beta=1-a/gamma, differentiating gamma*beta*h(beta)+2gamma*integral_beta^rho h gives -gamma*log((1-beta)/(1-rho)); the value at beta=rho is zero. This verifies the stated repaired entropy formula. No final rate counterexample is established.

problems.independent_check: The regularized problem retains epsilon<=v_prime<=1-epsilon. With epsilon=delta=0.1, H=u/10+u^2/1000, lambda=100, v>=0.1*(u-delta) gives H-v<=0.011. Integrating the claimed derivative requires at least90exp(-1.1), while the endpoint h_prime difference is at most2log9. The contradiction also persists for smaller positive delta<=0.1.
problems.counterevidence_and_impact: The false equality drives convexity/contact and the upper-bound optimizer. A variational inequality is needed. The repair certificate has dpsi>=0 supported on contact, w-vstar<=0 there, left endpoint zero, right psi=0 or psi<=0 with w-vstar<=0. A zero-slope endpoint uses O(delta*abs(log delta)); the intended optimizer survives after the local translation corrections.

problems.independent_check: (5.6) replaces the log indicator by a finite indicator-weighted cost. A zero indicator remains zero in the subsequent minimum; discarding it cannot imply a positive constrained infimum. The superexponential exclusion must be retained. Center-dependent arbitrarily small balls about a dense interior set need not cover the compact boundary. A positive atomic empirical measure also fails the mass-on-interval<=length condition defining M_R.
problems.counterevidence_and_impact: Lemma3.4 gives the relevant uniform quenched flux estimate. Entropy-dual neighborhoods at every center and lattice-cell smearing provide a repair route, whose neighborhood extension remains to be stated. The displayed gap is central to(5.7) and Theorems2.7-2.8, not proof that the final rates are false.

problems.independent_check: At zrho=A+gamma*(2rho-1), the printed terminal affine branch jumps by2rho*A. Section6.1 prints the correct rho*(u-zrho)+G(zrho-A). Direct integration gives K1=-gamma*log(1-rho)-gamma*rho; the empty interval contributes -(A-gamma)*log(1-rho), explicitly restored in(5.11) and Step6. The first Prop6.1 candidate rho*u violates v(a)=0 at a=1,b=2,H=1+u^2,rho=1/2.
problems.counterevidence_and_impact: The correct forms are already used downstream. These remain local normalization defects, not an additional false ultimate rate.

problems.independent_check: The generator minus the printed compensator leaves2q*(exp(-lambda)-1)*a_minus. Under pinned equilibrium its mean is2q*(exp(-lambda)-1)*(1-rho), equal to-1/8 at p=3/4,rho=1/2,lambda=log2. Bounded jump rates justify the first-order expectation calculation.
problems.counterevidence_and_impact: Actual tilt(4.3) and Section8 use the correct sign, so those operative estimates survive.

problems.independent_check: At t=0, the stated decomposition with a conventional zero-start Poisson process forces chi0=0; stationarity forces chit=0 at each fixed t. But q>0 gives a negative first jump with probability q*(1-rho)*t+O(t^2).
problems.counterevidence_and_impact: Only the printed initialization/formulation fails. A stationary coboundary or random offset is not excluded. The later proof is independent of that approximation.

problems.independent_check: A small smooth compact perturbation of the background, with sufficiently small derivative to remain a smooth entropy solution through time1, has strictly positive initial entropy and zero entropic dynamic cost. The printed positive-cost log-probability is impossible since log probability<=0.
problems.counterevidence_and_impact: The main bounds and entropy arguments use the correct negative sign.

problems.independent_check: The compactification keeps infinite coordinates infinite. The all-infinite configuration is invariant, but zeta(k) is not a finite bounded generator test. The printed invariant expectation needs bounded truncation and boundary-at-infinity terms.
problems.counterevidence_and_impact: This is explicitly an optional LLN proof. Tracy-Widom v2 pp1-3, with pTW=q,qTW=p, gammaTW=p-q and reflection X=1-x1, gives the right step profile and fixed-time speed. At q=0 the leading TASEP particle is a free rate-one Poisson process. Bounded drift and the scaled martingale imply uniform tightness. The imported Fredholm proof is not newly certified.
